about.title: Weed Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Weed sits at a rural crossroads where S Weed Boulevard, Rt 97, and I-5 carry a steady mix of local traffic, freight, and travelers passing through the mountains. Public records show a small but real number of injury collisions here each year, often clustering on Friday afternoons when work commutes and weekend travel overlap. When a crash happens, the aftermath can be disorienting — medical visits, missed work, and calls from insurance adjusters all at once. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect people hurt in Weed car accidents with independent attorneys who handle these cases directly, so you have someone reviewing the details before you say anything to an insurer that could affect your claim. There's no cost to get connected, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. Our goal is simply to make that first step easier during a stressful time.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a road maintained by Caltrans or Siskiyou County — is involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Affect Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly at fault, though your share of blame reduces the amount. Insurers often try to pin more fault on you than is fair, which is why an early, informed response matters.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic harm the way some states do. That makes it especially important to document your injuries thoroughly and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've talked to an attorney. Insurers sometimes use these statements to shift blame or minimize your injuries. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say and when.

items.question: What if my accident happened on I-5 or Rt 97, and the other driver was from out of town?
items.answer: Out-of-state or out-of-town drivers can complicate a claim, especially around insurance coverage and jurisdiction. An attorney familiar with Siskiyou County claims can help sort out where and how to file, and how to handle communication with an out-of-area insurer.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee and no payment unless you recover compensation. You can start the process with no financial risk.
